payload.body:
examiner (round 1): approach for the Task 2 exam, written to fleet/tests/exams/run_184/test_factory_judge.mjs (EXAM PATHS remap of the Proof's fleet/tests/test_factory_judge.mjs; ROOT is four levels up from the file, so nothing depends on cwd).

One assertion per leg, each labelled '(leg) [Mn]'. A fake `ask` records every call and answers canned answers in the replay's shapes ({type:'noul',noul}, {type:'choice',choice,confidence,probabilities}, {type:'score',score}); no socket, no real client. The seven severity thresholds, policy.task.k and policy.task.referee are all read off factory/policy.json at test time, never spelled as literals in the exam's expectations.

Three readings of the legs a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. Leg (a) pins M2__f1's question as containing `files.f1` AND `clauses[1]`. So the M-number in the KEY is 1-based over the clause array (M1 = clauses[0]) while the substitution into pairwise.instructions.question uses the 0-based array index — M2__f1 reads 'files.f1 ... clauses[1]', not 'clauses[2]'. M1's own coverage rule agrees (coverage[i] = max_j M<i+1>__f<j>), and leg (a)'s fake answers (0.2, 0.8, 0.5, 0.1 -> coverage [0.8, 0.5]) only come out right under that indexing. The exam encodes leg (a) verbatim.

2. The Machine pins no argument shape for readNote/readAmendment/readSupervisor, and leg (g) checks only their questions object and their resolved value. The exam therefore calls each with an object shaped by that set's own `state` key list in factory/questions.json (note: {title, claim, role, note, candidates}; amendment: {amendment:{...}, sibling:{...}}; supervisor: {inferred:{...}, observed:{...}}) and asserts NOTHING about the state those three send — only that each puts its set's questions once and resolves what `ask` answered.

3. Leg (g) says readNote/readAmendment/readSupervisor each resolve an object deep-equal to the answers the fake returned, so these readers do NOT flatten the way fleet/jev-questions.mjs's readers do; 'the flat answers object' in M4 means the answers object itself, unwrapped. The exam asserts deep equality with the answer objects as returned.

Leg (e) tries doc_or_prose_only at both 0 and 1 on BOTH review_difficulty rungs, not just the below-rung one: 76fdc03 removed exactly that OR from the referee gate, so both rungs are worth pinning under the leg's 'whatever doc_or_prose_only answers'.

payload.body:
Task 3 approach: factory/tools.mjs exports factoryTools({kata,projectId,task,candidates}) returning createSdkMcpServer({name:'factory',version,tools:[note,hand,settled,sibling_fact]}).

Resolution: fleet/node_modules is NOT on factory/'s upward resolution path (factory/ and fleet/ are siblings, no root node_modules), so the module loads the SDK and zod with a top-level-await loader that tries the bare specifier first, then ../fleet/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs (the path the task's Context names), then a createRequire anchored at fleet/package.json. One static-looking import in effect, robust to whichever layout Task 1's install leaves.

Per-clause: note -> kata.comment(projectId, task.uid, body) once, answers the uid the answer carried; hand -> one patchMetadata with {'work.attention':'needs-human','work.attention_msg':reason}; settled -> candidate membership checked here, patch value is a JSON STRING of {symbol,file,task:task.id} (metadata is flat+dotted, CONTRACT.md metadata-dotted-flat), a non-candidate makes NO kata call and answers 'not among' + every candidate; sibling_fact -> one kata.getIssue(uid), the text block is bare JSON of the issue's metadata so a reader can JSON.parse it, and a rejection answers 'no fact: ...' rather than rejecting.

The tool() definition array is also attached to the returned config as .tools so an exam can invoke handlers without an MCP client. I write no test file: fleet/tests/test_factory_tools.mjs is the peer's exam and fleet/ is frozen by my own Check proof.

payload.author: exam:3@run-184
payload.body:
examiner (round 1), approach: the exam lands at fleet/tests/exams/run_184/test_factory_tools.mjs (EXAM PATHS maps it off fleet/tests/test_factory_tools.mjs), plain node + node:assert/strict in the house style, ending in ALL TESTS PASSED.

Reading of leg (a). The Proof offers two routes to the four tool names — 'the instance's registered tool list, or the config's tool handlers exported for the exam'. I take the first: factoryTools' answer is the real createSdkMcpServer config, and its .instance carries the registered tool table. Measured against @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.275 in a scratch install: createSdkMcpServer({name,version,tools}) answers {type:'sdk', name, instance}, and instance._registeredTools is an object keyed by tool name whose entries carry a function .handler (older MCP server versions spell that .callback). So the exam reads the table off the instance and invokes entry.handler(args, {}) for legs (b)-(d). It does NOT invent a second export on factory/tools.mjs — Produces names only factoryTools, and an exam that accepted an invented export would grade a shape the contract never defined. To stay version-proof rather than pinned to one private field, the accessor tries _registeredTools/_tools/registeredTools and then any own property of the instance that is a non-empty object of handler-bearing entries; whichever it finds, the assertion is on the tool NAMES, not on the accessor.

The exam imports nothing but node builtins and ../../../../factory/tools.mjs — no zod, no MCP client, no network — so its only red at BASE is the absent module.

Why the fake's shapes are what they are: kata.comment answers the mutation projection (flat {uid, revision, short_id, ...}) exactly as fleet/kata-client.mjs projects it, so 'the comment's uid' is read off a flat .uid; kata.getIssue answers the ISSUE projection carrying .metadata, dotted-flat per CONTRACT's metadata-dotted-flat row. patchMetadata's real arity is (projectId, uid, patch, revision) but M2/M3 spell three, so the exam asserts the first three and says nothing about a revision argument.

One place the exam is tighter than the leg and looser than nothing: M3 spells the whole patch as { 'interface.settled': <JSON string> }, so the exam equals the patch's key set to exactly ['interface.settled'] and requires the value to be a string that JSON-parses to {symbol,file,task}. M3's 'every candidate name' is checked on a second server built with candidates ['catalog','ledger']; the leg's own single-candidate case is checked as the leg writes it.

examiner, round 1 done: fleet/tests/exams/run_184/test_factory_roles.mjs is written and red at BASE on leg (a)'s first assertion — `factory/roles/implement.md` exists — which is the absent implementation and nothing else. It imports no module (no sibling file is touched), spawns nothing, and writes nothing; it is a static read of the three role files.

Readings of legs a later session would otherwise reconstruct:

1. Word count is per-file and summed, not `cat | wc -w`. Leg (a)'s words are 'the sum of their whitespace-separated word counts'. The two differ by one per file that ends without a trailing newline, and the per-file sum is the larger — so the exam never passes something the Proof's Run: line would fail.

2. 'A sentence' in leg (b) is read as a maximal run of text bounded by . ! ? or a line break. A markdown bullet or heading is therefore a sentence too. This matters to the implementer: 'Post a hand-in note through the `note` tool naming what you exported.' passes, but splitting that across two sentences does not.

3. Stemming, where the leg's word has an obvious inflection: `iterate` accepts iterat*, `export` export*, `amendment` amendment*, `create` creat*, `invent` invent*, `note` note/notes, `rerun` also re-run. `only`, `until`, `both`, `listed`, `narration`, `Machine` and the five reply-shape tokens are whole words. `Machine` is case-sensitive, being the clause label.

4. Leg (d) is read literally: a line is checked only if it contains `git ` WITH the trailing space, and `not`/`never` are matched as substrings, so 'cannot' satisfies it. Note the consequence — a line writing the word as `\`git\`.` with no following space is not checked at all, which is the leg's own boundary, not a gap I introduced.

5. One hole in the Proof itself, recorded rather than patched: leg (b)'s `amendment` check ('contains the word `amendment`') is already satisfied by the `AMENDMENTS:` section literal the same leg requires, so a file that names the section but never tells the worker to declare a divergence still passes that assertion. I encoded the leg as written rather than tightening it — the exam is not mine to reshape — but a reviewer grading M2's 'declare a divergence as an amendment rather than hide it' should read the prose for it, since this exam cannot distinguish it. Every other leg was mutation-probed in a scratch tree (dup section literal, dropped only+listed, dropped iterate pair, dropped note+export, dropped Machine, dropped not+create, each of the three resolve rules, a missing reply-shape token, an injected grading word, an injected MUST, a 'run git add -A' line, and a 900-word overrun): all thirteen go red, and a plausible 273-word role set goes green.
